title: Ripple Effect Pressuring Global Stock Markets
description:
The orderly selloff we’ve been having just got a bit disorderly. The markets started the week feeling like it was a Manic Monday with stock futures sharply lower on extended concerns regarding China’s real estate sector.
Of particular interest is Hong Kong-listed Chinese developer Evergrande Group and whether Beijing will let the debt-laden firm fail. A default could mean potentially billions in losses for shareholders and bondholders around the world.
This is on top of continued concerns that there could be ripple effects for the rest of the global economy as the Chinese government continues to tap down on its real estate and other industries that are considered in need of reining in.
Meanwhile, lawmakers in Washington continued debating an increase to the government’s borrowing limits. The House is set to vote this week on the debt ceiling and a stopgap spending measure to keep the government operating past the end of the fiscal year, which ends on September 30.
The upshot was a clear risk-off tone to the market. Following sell-offs on Friday and this morning, the question now is will this become a prolonged number of sell-off days or will this signal a buying opportunity. 
Stuck In The September Doldrums
Monday morning’s sell-off is a continuation to last week’s action, which ended on a down note as the major indices hit a roadblock following a rebound on Thursday. Selling was pretty widespread across the S&P 500 Index (SPX), with only Health Care and Consumer Staples even coming close to the unchanged mark. Those two sectors tend to be more defensive in nature.
Overall, September continues to live up to its bad reputation as historically the weakest month of the year. But that doesn’t mean it can’t rebound. One thing we continued to see even during Friday’s worst moments was some “buying the dip” down near the 50-day moving average for the SPX. That level was near 4436 going into the end of last week and the SPX closed just below it at 4432.76. This morning the E-mini S&P 500 Index futures (/ES) are trading lower which could mean the SPX could start the week below the 50-day MA. The SPX has generally bounced every time it’s fallen to the 50-day MA so far this year. Hopefully, this means after two days of selloffs, there’s a chance we’ll rebuild from there.  
If the 50-day MA gets taken out in a major way (meaning several closes in a row below it), then it might be harder to find enthusiastic buyers and perhaps there could be a test of the 100-day MA down near 4326. That kind of move, interestingly enough, would get the SPX into basically a 5% downturn from its all-time high of 4545 set in early September. Many analysts have noted how long it’s been since the market had a 5% move lower. There hasn’t been one this year, which is kind of weird considering it’s something experienced nearly every year at some point.
For the market to avoid that, it would probably help if it got some support from the mega-caps, but that didn’t happen late last week. The recent stretch has been a very tough one for the “trillion-dollar-plus” club, with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) taking a hit almost every day lately despite last week’s Apple Event where the company introduced new products. Shares are down about 7% from the all-time high. When the mega-caps are suffering, the SPX tends to get hurt, too, because the Apples and Microsofts (NASDAQ: MSFT) of the world have a massive weighting in the index. (Friday Market Open) Another day, another round of earnings reports. However, the dark cloud of rising interest rates appears to be hanging over investors as equity index futures point to a lower open. Even the “happiest place on earth” is facing another storm.
Potential Market Movers
Disney (DIS) has lost ground after revelations from Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) that its streaming service had lost subscribers and expects to lose many more. Now, the Florida legislature has voted to end Disney’s 50-year-old special self-governing district by June 1, 2023. The self-governing district allowed Disney to collect taxes, provide emergency services, and build new structures without local government approval. However, according to CNBC, the move may result in Florida taxpayers absorbing a $1 billion bond debt. There’s also the question of whether Florida will now be entitled to the additional tax revenue that the special Disney district was collecting as well as building and permit fees. Obviously, there’s a lot more to come on this story and how it will  affect Disney going forward.
While Disney is dealing with its own issues, the rest of the market will likely be undergoing another revaluation. Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s more hawkish tone on Thursday caused stocks to fall and yields to rise. On the bright side, the 10-year Treasury yield (TNX) was down about 16 basis points in premarket trading which may take some of the sting out of valuation calculations.

The U.S. dollar index (DXY), as tracked by the Invesco DB USD Index Bullish Fund ETF (NYSE:UUP), dropped below the key 100 mark on Thursday, plunging to its weakest levels since April 2022, as softer-than-expected consumer and producer inflation encouraged traders to scale back bets of more than one rate hike by the Federal Reserve this year. 
Consumer price inflation fell to 3% year on year in June, the slowest rate since March 2021, a full percentage point lower than in May and well below the predicted 3.1%. The dollar came under pressure following a steep decline in U.S. Treasury yields, with the policy-sensitive two-year Note yield falling 20 basis points to 4.66% in the previous two sessions.

The dollar has suffered even greater losses versus emerging-market currencies, such as the Mexican peso (MXN) and the Chilean peso (CLP), which are up 20% and 18%, respectively, since their lows in 2022.

title: 2 Strong Buy Momentum Stocks Worth Owning as S&P 500 Hits New Highs
description: As the S&P 500 reaches new record highs, two momentum stocks stand out: Palantir Technologies and Newmont Goldcorp. Palantir is benefiting from the AI boom, while Newmont is gaining from rising gold prices.

title: Prepare for a Silver Surge: Best Mining Stocks to Watch Now
description: Investors are turning to silver as an alternative to gold amid the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike. The article highlights several silver mining stocks and ETFs that could benefit from the surge in silver prices.

title: New Drill Results from Alaska Project Positive
description: US GoldMining's initial drill results from its Whistler gold-copper project in Alaska were positive, confirming continuity of high-grade mineralization and the presence of two mineralization types. The company's experienced management team and the project's potential for additional high-grade mineralization make it an attractive investment opportunity.

title: Newmont Strikes ~$1B Deal For Akyem Sale, Focus Sharpens on Tier 1 Assets
description: Newmont Corporation has sold its Akyem mine in Ghana to Zijin Mining Group for up to $1 billion in cash, focusing on its Tier 1 assets. The proceeds will strengthen Newmont's balance sheet and support capital returns to shareholders.

title: Gold Miners Could Be on the Verge of an Epic Quarter
description: Gold miners are expected to report record-breaking earnings in Q3 2024 due to soaring gold prices and slightly lower mining costs. This could attract more fund inflows into the undervalued gold mining sector.

title: Why Is Gold Mining Dividend Stock Newmont Selling Off With Gold Prices at All-Time Highs?
description: Newmont, a gold mining company, saw its stock price drop despite gold prices being at all-time highs. This was due to the company's earnings falling short of expectations, with costs outpacing sales growth. The article suggests that investors may be better off investing in gold ETFs rather than gold mining stocks.

title: Newmont Seeks To Extend Largest Australian Mine Until 2050
description: Newmont has applied to extend the permit for its Cadia operation, Australia's largest underground mine, until 2050. The extension would secure over 2,100 local jobs and contribute significantly to the regional economy.

title: NATIONS ROYALTY ANNOUNCES TRADING ON THE FRANKFURT STOCK EXCHANGE UNDER SYMBOL Y96
description: Nations Royalty Corp. announced that its common shares are now trading on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the symbol 'Y96'. The listing is expected to increase the company's visibility and facilitate investment from European investors.

title: Here's Why Newmont Corporation Stock Fell 15% in October
description: Newmont Corporation's quarterly earnings were mostly in line with expectations, but rising costs, particularly for labor and energy, led to a 15% drop in the stock price. The company's Costs Applicable to Sales per ounce of gold produced increased by over 30% year-to-date, which raised concerns about future profitability.

title: White Gold Corp. Announces Significant Increase in Mineral Resources to 1,203,000 oz Gold Indicated and 1,116,600 oz Gold Inferred at the White Gold Project, Yukon, Canada
description: White Gold Corp. announced a significant increase in mineral resources at its White Gold project in Yukon, Canada, with 1,203,000 oz of gold in the Indicated Resource category and 1,116,600 oz of gold in the Inferred Resource category.

title: Newmont Sells Mine For $795 Million, Barrick Expands Reserves; Top Miners Unfazed By Underperformance
description: Newmont sells its Éléonore mine in Quebec for $795 million, continuing its strategy to focus on Tier 1 assets. Barrick expands its Nevada Fourmile project with significant gold reserves. Despite underperformance, the top miners remain unfazed as they adapt their strategies to industry challenges.

title: Newmont Sells Colorado Mine For $275 Million, Refocuses On Gold, Copper
description: Newmont Corporation has sold its Cripple Creek & Victor mine in Colorado to SSR Mining Inc. for up to $275 million, as part of its strategy to divest non-core assets and focus on its Tier 1 gold and copper operations.

title: 5 Gold Stocks Set to Shine as Yellow Metal's Rebound Sets Stage for Bullish 2025
description: Gold has rebounded strongly in recent weeks, suggesting 2025 could be another bullish year for the yellow metal. The article highlights 5 major gold stocks that could benefit from this potential rise, with Barrick Gold standing out as an undervalued opportunity.

title: White Gold Corp. Announces Upsize to Private Placement
description: White Gold Corp. is increasing the size of its previously announced non-brokered private placement from $4,500,000 to approximately $5,250,000. The company plans to use the proceeds to fund its exploration activities in the White Gold District.

title: Blockchain in Mining Strategic Intelligence Report 2024 with Focus on Supply Chain Management as the Main Use Case
description: The report discusses the growing importance of blockchain in the mining sector, with supply chain management being the main use case. It highlights the challenges and benefits of blockchain adoption, as well as the market size and growth forecasts.
